definitions.explanation: A set of symptoms that regularly occur together and are treated as one named condition. Also used loosely of recurring social or behavioral patterns, as English does with "syndrome."

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{症候群|しょうこうぐん}が{報告|ほうこく}された。
examples.english: A new syndrome has been reported.

examples.japanese: {医師|いし}は{睡眠時無呼吸|すいみんじむこきゅう}{症候群|しょうこうぐん}を{疑|うたが}っている。
examples.english: The doctor suspects sleep apnea syndrome.

examples.japanese: この{症候群|しょうこうぐん}は{原因|げんいん}がはっきりせず、{治療法|ちりょうほう}も{確立|かくりつ}されていない。
examples.english: The cause of this syndrome is unclear, and no treatment has been established.

examples.japanese: {連休明|れんきゅうあ}けに{会社|かいしゃ}へ{行|い}きたくなくなるのを、{冗談|じょうだん}まじりに{五月病|ごがつびょう}{症候群|しょうこうぐん}と{呼|よ}ぶ{人|ひと}もいる。
examples.english: Some people jokingly call the reluctance to go to work after a long holiday a "May blues syndrome."

notes:
Formed from {症候|しょうこう} (symptom) + {群|ぐん} (group). Attaches to the end of a condition's name, exactly where English puts "syndrome."

COMMON COMBINATIONS:
- {睡眠時無呼吸|すいみんじむこきゅう}{症候群|しょうこうぐん}: sleep apnea syndrome
- {過敏性腸|かびんせいちょう}{症候群|しょうこうぐん}: irritable bowel syndrome
- ダウン{症候群|しょうこうぐん}: Down syndrome

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {症状|しょうじょう}: symptom — a single sign of illness, whereas {症候群|しょうこうぐん} is the whole named cluster
- 〜{病|びょう}: disease — used when the cause is known; a syndrome is named from its symptoms alone
